title: The Chart That Does Not Lie: One Model, a Window and a Terminal, and a Steady Signal That Stays Steady

questions.question: Why does one model work out the range, rather than each view?
options: So the two charts cannot disagree: a steady signal is flat in both or storm in both
questions.explanation: The steady signal was 1 of 13 rows and 1 of 130 pixel rows.

questions.question: A signal of 5 plus or minus 1e-6 has no minimum span. What do both charts show?
options: A storm: 11 of 13 rows of text and 119 of 130 pixel rows
questions.explanation: They lie together, because they share the range.

questions.question: Where is a spike in a terminal chart of 50 columns and a window of 200 pixels?
options: The same fraction across: column 35 of 50 and column 140 of 200

questions.question: Why does the window mark ticks and not write their labels?
options: Text in a picture depends on fonts, which differ between platforms and make a picture hard to compare
Labels are in the terminal only by accident
questions.explanation: The lesson says so under what it does not do.

questions.question: What does add_sample do to repaint?
options: Asks for a repaint, which Qt does once when the loop is free
questions.explanation: Lesson 10-11: ten thousand updates are one paint.

questions.question: What is the minimum span a choice about?
options: What counts as steady for this signal, which the chart cannot know
questions.explanation: 0.1 suits a temperature and not a microvolt.
